summary: Fixed O(n^2) chunk-boundary search in _snap_end: the unbounded text.find(marker, lo) calls scanned the entire remaining string for every window, making _split_text quadratic on newline-free text (10MB single-line uploads). Bounded both find calls to the +-20% tolerance window [lo, hi + len(marker)], which preserves exact output semantics (a match at position p fits the slice iff p <= hi, identical to the old condition) while doing constant work per window. Added a regression test asserting exact boundaries and a <5s wall-clock guard on a 4MB single-line split.
notes: Root cause: _snap_end called text.find(marker, lo) and text.find(marker, position + 1) with no upper bound; on newline-free text each window performed 2 full scans of the remaining string -> O(n^2) (measured 5.04s/1MB, 23.31s/2MB, 77.23s/4MB before). Fix passes bound = hi + len(marker) to both finds; work per window is O(tolerance). Byte-identical output verified against the original implementation across 307 generated inputs x 5 parameter sets (paragraph breaks, single newlines, dense newlines, empty/short text, markers at window edges): 0 mismatches. Before/after: _split_text(text,100,20) 1MB 5.04s->0.036s, 2MB 23.31s->0.081s, 4MB 77.23s->0.149s (roughly linear); test_total_storage_limit_raises 473.2s->15.16s; full suite 140 passed in 15.56s pytest-time / 24.5s wall (139 pre-existing + 1 new test, no skips).
